=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/post_agent_workspace_guard.py
  Line or code reference: reconcile(), lines 265-289
  Problem: When any rejection exists, ALL newly created files (including legitimate ones) are moved to quarantine by the first loop (lines 268-270) and are NEVER restored in the else branch (lines 280-289). The else branch only processes individual rejected items for additional quarantine moves, but non-rejected created roots remain in quarantine permanently.
  Why it fails at runtime: If a model creates legitimate-new-source.txt alongside sitecustomize.py (malicious), both are quarantined upfront. The reconcile returns exit 20, the caller sets cmd_rc=78, and the legitimate file is silently lost — it does not appear in the next attempt's workspace snapshot. While the fail-closed security posture is correct, the collateral quarantine of safe files is an operational correctness gap: the report marks them as "quarantined" but they are indistinguishable from unauthorized files in the report output, and callers that inspect the report expecting to recover legitimate changes would need to manually reconstruct them from backup.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- scripts/post_agent_workspace_guard.py
  Line or code reference: _is_ignored(), line 168
  Problem: git check-ignore --no-index evaluates the path against ignore rules without consulting the Git index. A file that is tracked in the index but happens to match a .gitignore pattern returns exit code 0 (ignored), causing a false-positive "ignored-path" rejection.
  Why it fails at runtime: The workspace .gitignore may contain broad patterns (e.g., *.py in a data directory with force-added exceptions). A model modifying a force-added tracked file that also matches that ignore rule would be rejected, causing the entire editor attempt to fail with exit 20. The --no-index flag was chosen deliberately so that the guard catches files that are genuinely git-ignored (which is the correct threat model), but it also catches the narrower edge case where tracked files match ignore patterns. Swapping to plain check-ignore (without --no-index) would check the index first and return 1 for tracked files regardless of ignore rules, which is more precise for this use case.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- scripts/review_commit_changes.sh
  Line or code reference: run_review_validator_python(), lines 74-84
  Problem: Unlike the equivalent wrappers in check_resolver_diff.sh (run_isolated_validator_python, line 113ff which falls back to env -i python3 -I -S), implement_commit_changes.sh (run_implement_validator_python, line 55ff which falls back to env -i), and trusted_git_write.sh (run_trusted_validator_python, line 76ff which falls back to env -i), this wrapper fails with error when the sandbox helper is not executable rather than falling back to an isolated direct execution path.

- scripts/post_agent_workspace_guard.py
  Line or code reference: reconcile(), lines 265-289
  Problem: When the rejection path is taken, ALL newly created files (including legitimate ones) remain in quarantine permanently. The first loop at line 268-270 moves every created root to quarantine. The `if not rejected` branch at line 271 restores them. But the `else` branch at line 280 only iterates over rejected items — non-rejected created files stay in quarantine.
  Why it fails at runtime: If the model creates `safe.py` (legitimate) alongside `evil/sitecustomize.py` (malicious), both `safe.py` and `evil/` are moved to quarantine as created roots in step 1. The reconcile then returns exit 20, the caller fails the run (cmd_rc=78 / exit 78 in implement/repair paths), and on the next attempt the workspace snapshot has no `safe.py`. The editor's legitimate work is silently lost as collateral damage. This contradicts the linked-issue requirement "preserve authorized new files" and creates a denial-of-work failure mode that retry cannot recover from because each retry takes a fresh snapshot from a workspace missing the previous legitimate output.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- scripts/post_agent_workspace_guard.py
  Line or code reference: _is_ignored(), lines 166-176
  Problem: `git check-ignore --no-index` classifies paths against ignore rules without consulting the index, so a tracked file whose path matches an ignore pattern returns exit code 0 (ignored) instead of the `git check-ignore` (no `--no-index) "not ignored because tracked" exit code 1.
  Why it fails at runtime: Many real-world repos use broad ignore patterns (`*.tmp`, `*.bak`, build/, dist/, vendor/, etc.) combined with `git add -f` for tracked exceptions (force-added `.gitattributes`, generated `.tmp` files committed intentionally, vendor snapshots). When the model modifies a force-added tracked file whose name matches an ignore pattern, the guard classifies the change as "ignored-path" and rejects the entire attempt (exit 20), failing a legitimate edit. This is a broader class than the existing `unsupported-object` rules because it can affect any tracked file in a directory with a broad ignore pattern.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- scripts/post_agent_workspace_guard.py
  Line or code reference: reconcile rejection filter, lines 252-265
  Problem: The `hidden-path` reason rejects every dot-prefixed path component except `.github`. This blanket rule fires on tracked dotfiles the model is legitimately allowed to modify (`.gitattributes`, `.gitignore`, `.editorconfig`, `.env.example`, `.tool-versions`, `.python-version`, `Dockerfile.devcontainer`).
  Why it fails at runtime: A model that legitimately edits `.gitattributes` to register a new diff driver, or `.env.example` to document a new env var, will have the entire change quarantined as `hidden-path` and the attempt will fail. The rule conflates "hidden from `ls`" with "untrusted", but most hidden configuration files are tracked intentionally and the security boundary is Git tracking, not the leading dot.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

  Expected change site: scripts/post_agent_workspace_guard.py reconcile() — the `else` branch (rejection path) at lines 280-289
  Evidence of absence: When any rejection exists, the loop at line 280 iterates only over rejected items. There is no path that restores non-rejected entries from the quarantine dir back to the workspace. Step 1 unconditionally moved every created root to quarantine; step 2 (the `if not rejected` branch) was the only restore path. The bug above documents that authorized new files are not preserved when an unrelated unauthorized artifact appears in the same reconcile pass, contradicting the explicit preservation requirement.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
